lesson-word-missing.title: Lesson words with no dictionary entry
lesson-word-missing.why: A lesson lists a word id that words.json doesn't have, so the card can't show.

lesson-word-no-sentence.title: Lesson words with no example sentence
lesson-word-no-sentence.why: Taught words should have at least one example sentence. Tatoeba, Wiktionary and JESC had none for these.

lesson-word-furigana.title: Lesson words whose furigana doesn't spell the word
lesson-word-furigana.why: The furigana pieces put together should give back the word exactly.

lesson-word-duplicate.title: The same word taught twice
lesson-word-duplicate.why: Two lesson words share the spelling and the first meaning, so they'd be two cards for one thing.

lesson-word-rarer-homophone.title: Lesson words that may be the wrong dictionary entry
lesson-word-rarer-homophone.why: Another entry written and read the same way is more common, so the lesson may teach the rare meaning (ロケット as "locket" instead of "rocket").

lesson-word-junk.title: Junk words still in a lesson
lesson-word-junk.why: Words marked junk (a wrong dictionary match) shouldn't be taught.

word-lone-kana.title: Single-kana words outside the lessons
word-lone-kana.why: A lone kana as a word is usually a wrong dictionary match (ト as "note G"). Check these aren't shown as cards.

kanji-no-reading.title: Kanji with no reading
kanji-no-reading.why: No on or kun reading to teach.

kanji-no-words.title: Kanji with fewer than 2 example words
kanji-no-words.why: Each kanji should show a few words that use it.

kanji-word-missing.title: Kanji pointing at words that don't exist
kanji-word-missing.why: A kanji's word list has an id that words.json doesn't have.

kanji-no-strokes.title: Kanji with no stroke order
kanji-no-strokes.why: KanjiVG has no strokes for these.

kanji-not-taught.title: Kanji in no lesson
kanji-not-taught.why: Every Joyo kanji should be in a lesson.

lesson-kanji-missing.title: Lessons listing kanji that don't exist

kanji-reading-no-word.title: On readings with no example word
kanji-reading-no-word.why: Kun readings often have no word of their own, but an on reading with none can't be shown in use.

radical-name.title: Radicals without exactly one name
radical-name.why: Each radical should have exactly one name (Lucas's rule).

radical-unused.title: Radicals no kanji uses
radical-unused.why: A radical in a lesson that no taught kanji contains doesn't help learn anything.

radical-used-in-missing.title: Radicals pointing at kanji that don't exist

sentence-translation.title: Sentences with a missing or untranslated English line
sentence-translation.why: The English is empty or still has Japanese in it.

items.ja: そうです。日本語ではウェートレスは英語の"waitress"と"weightless"にも該当する。でも"waitress"という意味が普通だね。
items.en: That's correct. In Japanese, ウエートレス corresponds both to the English "waitress" and "weightless". However, "waitress" is the more usual meaning.

sentence-bad-link.title: Sentences linking to missing words
sentence-bad-link.why: A tappable word in the sentence points at nothing.

sentence-duplicate.title: The same Japanese sentence more than once
sentence-duplicate.why: Usually harmless (different sources), listed so they can be merged.

story-odd-characters.title: Story text with damaged characters
story-odd-characters.why: Look-alike radicals (⼈ for 人) or vertical-only punctuation (︒ for 。) from the PDF's fonts. They look right but don't link to any word.

story-word-missing.title: Story words with no dictionary entry
story-word-missing.why: The story links the word, but words.json doesn't have it, so it can't be tapped or counted.

story-jumbled.title: Story text that may be jumbled
story-jumbled.why: Half or more of the character pairs never appear in real Japanese. Usually side notes, picture labels or furigana read in the wrong order; place-name lists also land here.
